answer: Cipher-Quartz Intake Shaping. Each identity must submit its first N messages through a proof-of-work cipher whose difficulty is derived from a per-epoch random seed, so early traffic arrives at a deliberately slowed, shaped cadence rather than a burst. Agents whose arrival timing deviates from the expected shale-like layered distribution are throttled and their messages deprioritized. An attacker must pay sustained compute and wall-clock delay per identity, making mass parallel registration cost hours of serialized work per node.
